name: Stripe
statusNote: Still private as of Oct 2026; no IPO. Feb 2026 employee tender offer at $159B; John Collison said an IPO is not among top priorities ('a solution in search of a problem').
oneLiner: Programmable financial services / payments infrastructure for internet businesses, pushing into agentic commerce and stablecoins.
founders: Patrick and John Collison (Irish brothers, previously founded Auctomatic).
talentSignals: Widely regarded as one of the strongest engineering cultures in fintech; founders highly visible (Patrick Collison ~1.8M X followers).
research: Engineering blog and some open-source tooling; not a research-output company.
traction: Total payment volume $1.9T in 2025, up 34% YoY (https://www.cnbc.com/2026/02/24/stripe-value-stock-sale-tender-offer.html). Self-funding business per John Collison.
moat: Dominant developer-first payments network, massive volume/data, broad product suite, distribution with nearly every AI company.
risks: Not an AI-native company; payments competition (Adyen, PayPal); valuation via tenders rather than primary rounds.
notes: Bloomberg says the 2025 mark was $106.7B (vs CNBC's $91.5B Feb 2025 tender) — different reference transactions. Revenue/ARR not disclosed; not found. Not a startup in the usual sense; probably belongs in a 'mega private' bucket.

name: Ramp
statusNote: Still private as of Oct 2026. Sep 2026: Bloomberg reported early talks to raise ~$1B at ~$60B (not closed as of reporting).
oneLiner: Corporate cards, spend management, bill pay and AI finance automation; positions itself as infrastructure to govern AI/token spend.
founders: Eric Glyman (CEO) and Karim Atiyeh (co-CEO since Jun 2026, ex-CTO); previously co-founded Paribus (acquired by Capital One). Rahul Sengottuvelu became CTO.
talentSignals: Leadership change Jun 2026: Atiyeh moved to co-CEO, Rahul Sengottuvelu to CTO (https://www.laplaceatlas.com/stories/ramp-is-in-early-talks-to-raise-1-billion-at-a-60-billion-valuation-87c4a6cb)
Known for high-velocity engineering culture; founders have large X followings.

rounds.leads: ICONIQ, GIC, Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan

research: Product/engineering blog; little formal research output.

xPosts.author: eglyman
xPosts.summary: Glyman announces $750M raise at $44B: 'Last time we grew this fast, we were 1/20th the size'; intelligence as third pillar of spend.

xPresence: @eglyman ~391k followers, @karimatiyeh ~201k, @tryramp ~43k (fxtwitter, Oct 2026). Funding announcements regularly reach 1M+ views.
traction: 70,000+ customers (Visa, Uber, Shopify, Anduril, Figma, Notion, Cursor), $200B annualized purchase volume, positive free cash flow, 3,200+ customers at $100k+ (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/ramp-raises-series-f-at-44-billion-valuation-302791103.html). TPV +170% YoY in Mar 2026 (https://techfundingnews.com/ramp-eyes-1b-series-g-at-60b-valuation-just-three-months-after-hitting-44b/). Main rival Brex sold to Capital One for ~$5.15B.
moat: Spend data and payments network, multi-product attach, cash-flow positive scale; rival Brex absorbed by Capital One.
risks: Card interchange dependence; fintech regulation; competition from banks and Rippling/Navan spend tools; rich multiple (~30-40x revenue).
notes: Bloomberg's $1.5B run-rate figure is reported, company officially says 'over $1B'. $60B round was in talks as of Sep 2026; not confirmed closed. Headcount not found.

name: Rippling
statusNote: Still private as of Oct 2026; CEO said no immediate IPO plans (May 2025). Secondary trades reported below Series G price in 2026.
oneLiner: Unified HR, IT and finance (payroll, benefits, device management, spend) platform built on a single employee graph, now pushing Rippling AI agents.
founders: Parker Conrad (previously founded Zenefits) and Prasanna Sankar.
talentSignals: Serial founder CEO with large following; aggressive compound-startup product strategy.
Ongoing litigation with Deel over alleged corporate espionage (https://www.briefs.co/news/judge-pares-back-deel-s-case-while-greenlighting-parts-of-ri/)

rounds.leads: Elad Gil, Sands Capital, GIC, Goldman Sachs Alternatives, Baillie Gifford, YC (participants)

research: Little public research output; product company.
xPresence: @parkerconrad ~451k followers (fxtwitter, Oct 2026); posts frequently and combatively (Deel, Runlayer).
traction: ARR over $1B growing 78% YoY with growth accelerating three straight quarters (Parker Conrad, Apr 2026). Reuters reported 20,000+ customers in 2025.
moat: Employee-graph platform with many attached products; high switching costs in payroll/HRIS.
risks: Deel litigation; secondary pricing below last round (~$13B, https://www.hustlefund.vc/post/angel-squad-rippling-pre-ipo-shares-what-accredited-investors-should-know-in-2026); crowded HCM market.
notes: A $250M 'Series H' (Aug 2026, Coatue lead) appears only on aggregator FundBat and is not corroborated by press; excluded. Conrad said on a podcast they are not currently fundraising but expect to within 12 months. Headcount ~6,000 per a Conrad X post seen via a mirror (not verified via fxtwitter), so headcount left null.

name: Glean
statusNote: Still private as of Oct 2026; no S-1 filed.
oneLiner: Permissions-aware enterprise search and AI agents platform ('Work AI') over a company's knowledge graph.
founders: Arvind Jain (CEO; ex-Google distinguished engineer, co-founder of Rubrik) with ex-Google engineers (T.R. Vishwanath, Piyush Prahladka, Tony Gentilcore).
talentSignals: Founder previously co-founded Rubrik (IPO 2024); heavy ex-Google search engineering team.
research: Technical blog output on enterprise search/RAG and knowledge graphs; no notable papers found.
traction: $300M ARR (May 2026), 3x in ~15 months; customers include Databricks, Reddit, Pinterest, Samsung (TechCrunch). Pitches ~30% token-spend reduction via its context graph.
moat: Connectors + permissions-aware knowledge graph across hundreds of SaaS apps; enterprise trust.
risks: Heavy competition from Microsoft Copilot, Google, OpenAI/Anthropic enterprise products, Atlassian, Salesforce; valuation flat since Jun 2025.
notes: Aggregator claims of an Aug 2026 $768M round (likely total funding) and a $6.4B Sep 2026 item (appears to be a different US-Israeli browser startup) are not corroborated; ignored. Acquired Aryn (Mar 2026) per PitchBook.

name: Hex
statusNote: Still private as of Oct 2026; last disclosed round Series C May 2025; product shipping actively through Sep 2026.
oneLiner: AI-native collaborative data workspace combining notebooks, BI, apps and data agents.
founders: Barry McCardel (CEO), Caitlin Colgrove (CTO), Glen Takahashi (Chief Architect) — all ex-Palantir.
research: Product changelog and data blog; modest public technical content; no notable papers or large OSS.
traction: Thousands of orgs incl. Reddit, StubHub, HubSpot, Cisco, Figma, Anthropic, Rivian, NBA (BusinessWire, May 2025). Partnership with ClickHouse (Mar 2026); frequent agent/generative-app releases (changelog).
moat: Strong product in notebooks+BI; Snowflake/Databricks partnerships; but category crowded.
risks: Competition from Databricks/Snowflake native notebooks, Deepnote, frontier-lab data agents; small scale vs peers.
notes: Series C valuation not officially disclosed (GetLatka claims ~$400M — unverified, excluded). No ARR disclosed; not found. Not a strong fit for an 'AI startup' ranking — it's a data tooling company with AI features.

name: Harvey
statusNote: Still private as of Oct 2026; raised $550M at $15.5B on 2026-09-09.
oneLiner: AI platform and agents for law firms and in-house legal teams (research, drafting, due diligence, contract analysis).
founders: Winston Weinberg (CEO, ex-O'Melveny & Myers litigator) and Gabe Pereyra (ex-DeepMind / Google Brain / Meta AI researcher).
talentSignals: Four acquisitions in 2026 incl. Guardrails AI (https://saassentinel.com/2026/09/10/harvey-raises-550m-at-15-5b-valuation-as-legal-ai-arr-tops-400m/)
Released first in-house post-trained open-weight model 'Harvey Tenet' (built on Kimi K3 with Fireworks) (https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/09/harvey-hits-15-5b-valuation-months-after-reaching-11b/)
research: Harvey Tenet post-trained open-weight legal model; Harvey LAB (Legal Agent Benchmark); legal AI blog output.
traction: 3,000+ customer orgs (up from ~1,300 in March 2026); 80% of Am Law 100; five of Fortune 10 legal teams (Harvey blog, TNW).
compute: Post-training via Fireworks on open-weight base models.
moat: Category leader in legal AI with deep law-firm penetration and workflow/data integrations.
risks: Competition from Legora (raised $600M Series D), Thomson Reuters/CoCounsel, frontier labs; ~39x ARR multiple.
notes: Bloomberg/TNW report $15.6B, company says $15.5B. Total raised >$1.55B. Headcount not found.

name: Sierra
statusNote: Still private as of Oct 2026; $950M Series E May 2026.
oneLiner: Enterprise platform for customer-facing conversational AI agents (chat and voice), priced on outcomes.
founders: Bret Taylor (OpenAI board chair, ex-Salesforce co-CEO, ex-Facebook CTO, co-creator of Google Maps) and Clay Bavor (ex-Google VP, led AR/VR and Labs).
talentSignals: Hired Julia Brau Donnelly (ex-Pinterest CFO) as CFO (via Bret Taylor post mirrored on TwStalker).
research: Published tau-bench (τ-bench) agent benchmark, widely used by frontier labs for tool-use evals; research blog.

xPosts.author: btaylor
xPosts.summary: Sierra hit $200M ARR: seven quarters to $100M, two more quarters for the next $100M.

xPresence: @btaylor ~162k followers, @claybavor ~31k (fxtwitter, Oct 2026). Milestone posts get 100k-500k views.
traction: Serves 40%+ of Fortune 50; billions of customer interactions (https://sierra.ai/blog/better-customer-experiences-built-on-sierra). Newcomer source says 'well-surpassed $200M' by Aug 2026.
moat: Founder brand and enterprise distribution, outcome-based pricing, deep deployments with forward-deployed engineers.
risks: Crowded category (Decagon, Salesforce Agentforce, Fin/Intercom acquired by Salesforce, frontier labs); ~80x ARR multiple; Taylor also OpenAI chair (conflict optics).
notes: Sierra itself said 'over $15B'; CNBC reported $15.8B post-money. Headcount not found. tau-bench is from 2024 (my prior knowledge; star count not checked).

name: Decagon
statusNote: Still private as of Oct 2026; Series D Jan 2026.
oneLiner: AI agents ('AI concierge') for enterprise customer support across chat, email and voice.
founders: Jesse Zhang (CEO; previously founded Lowkey, acquired by Niantic; ex-Google) and Ashwin Sreenivas (ex-Palantir; previously founded Helia).
traction: $100M+ annualized revenue (Aug 2026); 100+ new enterprise customers in 2025 incl. Avis Budget Group, Block, Deutsche Telekom, Mercado Libre; Q2 2026 revenue +~50% QoQ per CEO (LinkedIn).
moat: Product-led deployment (less reliance on forward-deployed engineers); some enterprise lock-in.
risks: Number two behind Sierra with ~1/3 the funding; Salesforce/Fin, Zendesk and frontier labs in market.
notes: Headcount not found. No verified X posts collected.

name: Rogo
statusNote: Still private as of Oct 2026; Series D Apr 2026 plus ~$30M strategic bank investments Sep 2026.
oneLiner: Agentic AI platform for investment banks, asset managers and PE firms (decks, models, research; agent 'Felix').
founders: Gabriel Stengel (CEO, ex-Lazard / Guggenheim banker) with Rahul Rekhi (President) and John Willett.
talentSignals: Embeds forward-deployed bankers and engineers inside clients (https://rogo.com/news/series-d)
Nine global banks on cap table incl. J.P. Morgan, Citi, Barclays, BNP Paribas, MUFG, Société Générale (https://rogo.com/news/strategic-investors)

rounds.leads: Barclays, BNP Paribas, Citi Ventures, MUFG, Société Générale

research: Some finance-benchmark content (e.g. 'BFB' benchmark mentioned on Rogo site); no notable papers found.
traction: 50,000+ professionals across 350+ firms (Sep 2026), up from 35,000 at 250+ firms (Apr 2026); clients include JPMorgan Chase and Bank of America. Expanding into wealth management (WSJ via Capital Brief).
moat: Deep integration and trust with regulated banks; strategic bank investors.
risks: Competition from frontier labs' finance products, Hebbia, AlphaSense, in-house bank tools; revenue not disclosed.
notes: Valuation $2B stated in company LinkedIn post and Capital Brief (citing WSJ). ARR/revenue not found. Total funding >$300M pre-strategic round.
